picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City seeks to convert 4.6 hectares of protective mangrove forest for $3.9B metro developed by Vingroup company
picked.body: All of it is classified as protection forest, made up of about 1.4 hectares of natural mangrove and 3.17 hectares of planted mangrove. The affected forest lies in An Thoi Dong and Can Gio communes, where the route passes through the buffer zone of the Can Gio Mangrove Biosphere Reserve but stays out of its core. The project is being developed by VinSpeed, a company of Vietnam's largest conglomerate Vingroup. The city approved it and named VinSpeed as investor on Dec. 5, 2025. The project broke ground two weeks later and is targeted for completion in 2028. The roughly 54 km double-track line will run from the Ben Thanh area in the city center to Can Gio, ending beside a land reclamation township on the coast. It is designed for a top speed of 350 kph. It will open with two stations, Ben Thanh and Can Gio, and a 39-hectare depot. Four intermediate stations will be considered at a later stage. The project has an estimated total investment of VND102.43 trillion ($3.94 billion), excluding site clearance, which the city budget covers. An updated feasibility study in May put site clearance at about VND9.83 trillion ($378 million), nearly VND3 trillion below the initial estimate. The People's Committee said the metro qualifies as an urgent transport project, a category that allows natural forest to be converted under current rules. It added that the line conforms to the city's master plans. VinSpeed has pledged to plant replacement forest. The project's environmental impact assessment has been approved.

picked.t: HS효성첨단소재, ‘T-1000급’ 탄소섬유로 북미 우주항공 시장 뚫는다
picked.body: 미국 애틀랜타에서 열린 ‘CAMX 2026’ HS효성첨단소재 부스에서 참관객들이 ‘탄섬(TANSOME®)’ 탄소섬유 제품을 살펴보고 있다. (사진=HS효성첨단소재) 인공위성 연료를 담는 고압용기와 하늘을 나는 드론의 몸체를 만드는 초고강도 탄소섬유가 북미 최대 첨단소재 무대 위에 오른다.  HS효성첨단소재는 22일부터 24일까지 미국 애틀랜타에서 열리는 북미 최대 복합재료 박람회 'CAMX 2026'에 참가해 글로벌 무대에서 기술력을 선보인다고 밝혔다. 행사 첫해인 2014년부터 빠짐없이 참가해온 HS효성첨단소재는 500여 개 기업과 7000여 명의 전문가가 결집할 것으로 예상되는 이번 행사에서 북미 파트너십을 한층 강화할 방침이다. 현장에서 HS효성첨단소재는 3K(3000 가닥) 탄소섬유 기반의 드론용 소재와 위성용 고압용기 등 고성능 신소재 라인업을 다채롭게 전시한다.  기존의 자동차 부품이나 스포츠 용품 등 범용 영역을 넘어서, 방산 및 우주항공 같은 고부가가치 미래 첨단 분야로 탄소섬유의 쓰임새를 확대해 나가는 시장 흐름에 발맞춘 전략이다. 핵심 경쟁력은 자체 기술로 일궈낸 독보적인 품질에 있다. 지난 2011년 국내 최초로 국산화에 성공한 탄소섬유 브랜드 '탄섬(TANSOME®)'을 비롯해, 2022년에는 미국과 일본에 이어 세계 세 번째로 초고강도 'H3065(T-1000급)' 개발을 완성했다.  자동차 품질 인증인 IATF 16949와 우주항공 분야 품질 표준인 AS9100 인증을 연이어 획득하며 국제적인 신뢰도까지 입증했다. 탄탄한 글로벌 제조 인프라 역시 강점으로 꼽힌다. 2013년 전북 전주 공장에서 첫 상업 생산을 시작한 이래 중국 생산 거점을 확보했으며, 2026년 하반기에는 베트남 공장 가동을 앞두고 있다.  HS효성첨단소재는 한국과 중국, 베트남을 잇는 3각 생산 체제를 바탕으로 안정적인 글로벌 공급망을 구축해 차별화된 소재 솔루션을 선사한다는 목표다.

picked.t: ‘고공행진 집값’ 베트남, 개발社 과도한 금융 의존 탓…자기자본 강화 필요
picked.body: 호치민시 푸미흥 지역의 한 아파트 단지.  베트남의 집값이 고공행진 중인 가운데 높은 집값이 부동산 개발사들의 과도한 금융 의존 때문이라는 지적이 나왔다. 베트남 감찰 당국은 부동산 프로젝트의 신용 의존도를 낮추고, 개발사들의 자기자본 비율을 높여야 집값을 낮출 수 있다고 지적했다. 현재 베트남 부동산 개발 분야 대출한도는 80~85%에 이른다. 베트남국가감사원은 건설부의 부동산사업법 개정안에 대한 의견 수렴에서 이 같이 지적했다. 국가감사원은 도시·주택 프로젝트 투자자 선정 기준을 강화할 것으로 권고하며, 특히 △재무역량 △지배구조 △프로젝트 운영 능력 요건을 더 엄격히 할 것을 건의했다. 국가감사원은 특히 부동산 개발사들의 자기자본비율을 높여야 한다고 강조했다. 국가감사원은 "현재 부동산 프로젝트에서 허용 중인 80~85%의 신용은 재무 부담, 결과적으로 사업 비용을 증가시켜 높은 주택 가격을 초래하고 있다”며 규정 변경이 필요하다는 의견을 제시했다. 국가감사원의 이 같은 지적은 최근 베트남 일부 대도시의 부동산 가격이 지속적으로 높은 수준을 유지하고 있는 가운데 공급 구조에서 수급 불균형이 심화하고 있는 상황에서 나와 더 많은 주목을 받고 있다. 아울러 베트남 부동산 시장은 올 들어 고금리 장기화로 인해 직격탄을 맞고 있다. 베트남 신용평가사 S&I레이팅스(S&I Ratings)에 따르면 현재 베트남 시행사·건설사의 은행 대출금리는 연 12%를 넘어서고 있다. 다만, 건설부는 자기자본 규정은 현행을 유지한다는 방침을 고수하고 있다. 현행법상 부동산 개발사는 사업지가 20헥타르 미만인 경우 총투자액의 최소 20%의 자기자본을, 20헥타르 이상인 경우 최소 15%를 보유해야 한다. 건설부는 “부동산 개발사 자기자본 규정은 이전 부동산사업법에서 지속적으로 유지되어온 것으로, 지난 수년간 실제 사례를 봐도 현재 기준이 실정에 부합하며, 역량 있는 투자자를 선별하는 데 효과를 보여왔다”며 “이 규정을 계승하는 것은 법률의 안정성을 보장하고, 기업의 영업 조건에 새로운 변동이나 차이를 발생시키지 않으며, 기업이 투자 과정에서 안정적으로 사업을 진행할 수 있는 여건을 조성하기 위한 것"이라고 밝혔다. 한편 베트남은행협회 역시 부동산 분야에 대한 구체적인 안전 비율 한도를 명확히 하거나, 정부가 시기별로 세부 규정을 마련하도록 할 것을 건의하고 나섰다. 건설부에 따르면 작년 말 기준 부동산 부문 대출잔액은 475조 동(약 182억7,140만 달러)에 달했는데, 이 중 부동산사업 대출이 약 258조 동(99억2,420만여 달러)으로 과반을 차지했다. 부동산채 발행액은 누적 39조8,000억 동(15억3,090만여 달러) 이상으로 전년 대비 44% 급증했다.

picked.t: Korean singer likens Phu Quoc basket boat ride to a thrill ride
picked.body: On Sept. 11, he uploaded a video lasting more than 40 minutes about his trip to Vietnam. He was on a vacation to celebrate his YouTube channel reaching 200,000 subscribers. Before the trip, the singer said he was worried because Phu Quoc is an island destination and a fortune teller had advised him to be careful around water this year. But nevertheless, he decided to go on the trip. In Phu Quoc, after enjoying coconut coffee, the singer took part in a lucky draw and won a challenge to experience a basket boat tour on the Cua Can River. The 45- to 60-minute tour costs VND200,000 (US$8) and includes a visit to a floating market, eating local fruits on the river, joining local residents for fishing, and watching basket boat performances. Lee praised the scenery along the Cua Can River, said the atmosphere was pleasant, and recommended that his fans should try a basket boat ride in Vietnam at least once. However, he became worried when the sky suddenly darkened and heavy rain forced the group to take shelter in a hut. After the rain eased, the group of Korean tourists continued their basket boat experience. One of the tour's activities involved local boatmen spinning the round basket boats rapidly in circles on the river, making the boats whirl around. Lee quickly became dizzy and nearly threw up, likening the dizzying ride to Disco Pang Pang, a popular thrill ride in South Korea. The singer also had a massage and exfoliation treatment, and headed to the Phu Quoc night market with VND100,000 (US$4) in hand. There, he tried horseshoe crab, durian, mangosteen, peanuts, and seafood noodle soup. He said the crab tasted similar to lobster and he shuddered when trying durian alongside two Vietnamese tourists. The video had attracted more than 1.2 million views and thousands of comments. Many viewers praised Phu Quoc's scenery and enjoyed Lee's experiences, while some said tourists should avoid visiting the island at this time because it is currently the rainy season. Phu Quoc has attracted a large number of South Korean tourists in recent years, with direct flights from South Korea to the island increasing, according to the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism (VNAT). In 2023, Yonhap News Agency described the island as the "Maldives of Vietnam" in a report on its appeal to Korean tourists. According to the VNAT, South Korea was Vietnam's second largest source of visitors in the first eight months of 2026 after mainland China, at some 2.76 million, and accounted for 17.3% of total international arrivals.

picked.body: Le Loi Street, leading toward the Saigon Opera House, is under water as traffic backs up. Quoc An, a local man, said the downtown area floods whenever heavy rain drags on. "These streets carry a lot of traffic, so once they flood, long jams form very easily," he said. picked.t: Hanoians struggle to navigate flooded streets without real-time warnings
picked.body: On the morning of Sept. 17, freshman Duy Phuc rode his motorbike from home in Ha Dong to the Hanoi National University of Education. Not knowing where to find flood updates, he followed his usual route. On To Huu Street, floodwaters rose above the vehicle's wheels and stalled the engine, forcing him to walk it back. A passing car sent up a wave of water that knocked him and his motorbike over. "If I had known this section was flooded, I would have taken another route or asked to be excused from class," he says. Vu Anh, 52, of Long Bien Ward, now checks social media groups whenever he needs to travel during heavy rain. But with message boards flooded even more than the roads, he struggles to determine which roads are usable. Referring to the same route, one person might report deep flooding while another might claim traffic is moving normally. "There is a lot of information, but you don't know which reports are accurate," Anh says. Anh used to depend on HSDC Maps, a flood-warning map developed by the Hanoi Drainage Company, but found that reports of newly flooded areas did not appear quickly enough to be of use. He recently tried the "Rain and Flood Map" feature on the iHanoi app. During the rain on Sept. 17, however, many users said some areas experiencing rain and flooding appeared dry on the map. The mini app was removed from iHanoi within just 14 days. For Xuan Ninh, 23, a ride-hailing driver, the most useful warnings come from VOV Traffic and a group chat with fellow drivers. When drivers encounter a flooded section, they share its location and photos so that those following them can avoid it. After once becoming trapped at an unreported flooded spot and having to cancel a ride, Ninh began checking the group chat or looking for livestreams from flooded locations before accepting a booking. "I just hope for something that tells us which roads are passable and which ones to avoid, instead of finding out only when we arrive," he says. The lack of information prompted Nguyen Dinh Mau, an artificial intelligence engineer at the Japan Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, to seek a solution. Mau returned to Hanoi in early September amid a bout of heavy rain. On his way from Thai Ha Street to 19-8 Hospital to visit a relative, he rolled up his pants and waded through knee-deep water past stalled vehicles. He realized that popular traffic apps could warn users about congestion, but flood information remained scattered across news reports and social media. In four days, he built Nuoc Len ("Rising Water"), a website that aggregates flood information. The system collects data from news outlets, VOV Traffic, meteorological sources, social media, and user reports. AI identifies locations and flood levels in the reports and plots them on a map. To filter out false reports and outdated images, the system cross-checks multiple reports from the same location, compares them with news reports and prioritizes data from government agencies, local authorities and specialized organizations, Mau explains. He launched the website on Sept. 17 as Hanoi was experiencing heavy rain, and it attracted hundreds of thousands of visits. He acknowledges that the current version only shows which locations are flooded and cannot yet automatically recommend alternative routes and that information from the public and social media may be inaccurate, and so the website can only act as a reference. Associate Professor Luu Duc Hai, director of the Institute for Urban Research and Infrastructure Development, says the fact that people have to scramble for information whenever heavy rain hits reveals a lack of real-time data and coordination among authorities. Current flood-monitoring systems do not have enough sensors, agencies do not synchronize their data, and community reports are not being used effectively, he says. He wants the city Department of Construction to develop a shared data platform that integrates flood maps with the intelligent transportation system. The Hanoi Drainage Company should provide data on rainfall, floodwater depth, and how long the water takes to recede, and the traffic police should combine flood data with the camera system to issue warnings and redirect traffic before motorists reach affected areas, he says. An effective map should show water depth, the extent of flooding, the time of the latest update, whether the water is rising or receding, and which types of vehicles can pass, he says. Eventually, the system should recommend alternative routes and accept verified reports from residents, he says. "A static flood map provides information only when it is already too late. A dynamic map must help people decide whether to continue, stop, or take another route." Mau says addressing the flood-information problem requires three elements working together: technology capable of issuing early warnings and automatically finding alternative routes; flood data connected to transportation and urban infrastructure system

picked.t: Living Exhibition opens Vietnam Festival of Creativity & Design 2026
picked.body: The exhibition at Nina Next Space marked the opening of the seventh Vietnam Festival of Creativity & Design (VFCD), organized by RMIT University Vietnam with individuals, organizations and businesses in the creative industries. Reflecting this year's "Living Festival" theme, the exhibition presents creative works as evolving processes rather than finished products. During the festival, works may be created, modified, performed or reinterpreted, allowing visitors to participate in their development. From exhibition to festival After six editions from 2019 to 2024, VFCD returns in 2026 as a biennial event with nearly 40 activities connecting creativity, research and community participation. The theme explores creativity as an evolving process shaped by interactions among people, ideas, disciplines and places. Professor Donna Cleveland, Dean of RMIT Vietnam's School of Communication & Design, said the university aims to connect different parts of the creative ecosystem through the festival. "As we open VFCD 2026 today, I would like to reaffirm RMIT University and the School of Communication & Design's commitment to this journey," she said. "We see ourselves as a convenor that brings together practitioners, students, researchers, businesses, cultural organizations, and communities. We hope to strengthen relationships across the creative ecosystem while linking Vietnam's creative community with regional and international networks." Rethinking exhibition-making The Living Exhibition uses a double-blind peer-review process, with each submission independently assessed by multiple international reviewers. Selected projects are grouped into four interconnected categories: Living Archives, Living Signals, Living Territories and Living Communities. The categories serve as thematic connections rather than fixed classifications, bringing together works from different creative disciplines. Associate Professor Lim Kok Yoong, Director of VFCD 2026 and Deputy Dean for Research and Innovation at RMIT Vietnam's School of Communication & Design, said the festival combines curation, research and experimentation. "VFCD is neither solely an arts festival nor an institutional or commercial industry event. It occupies a distinctive space between education, research, culture, industry, and public life," he said. "Its curatorial and peer-review processes allow VFCD to support experimentation and emerging practices while maintaining intellectual and academic rigors and creative freedom." VFCD 2026 comprises five interconnected tracks, with exhibitions, forums, laboratories, workshops, fieldwork and partner-led activities taking place across Ho Chi Minh City. The program brings together creative practice and research, education and professional work, public participation and international exchange.

picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City braces for continued heavy rain and flooding amid high tides
picked.body: The Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center projects total rainfall in the city to reach between 70 and 100 millimeters from Wednesday morning through 1 p.m. on Friday. Some areas could receive more than 150 mm of rain during this period. Widespread showers will persist Wednesday evening, compounding the impact of several torrential downpours that have battered the city since the beginning of the week. Tran Van Hung, deputy director of the center, noted the city is enduring a five-day stretch of widespread rain. Many areas recorded over 100 mm of rainfall between Sept. 21 and 22 alone. The highest concentration earlier this week was observed in the former Nha Be District, which received 249 mm. Meteorologists attribute the prolonged downpours to the interaction between the intertropical convergence zone and a low-pressure circulation moving inland from the sea. On Wednesday morning, a sudden 30-minute deluge struck the central business district, the former Binh Thanh District, and the former Thu Duc City area. This heavy rush-hour rain severely disrupted morning commutes and school drop-offs across the metropolis. Across the broader southern region, the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting expects 40 to 80 mm of rainfall from Wednesday morning through the night, with localized peaks exceeding 150 mm. Regional rainfall totals on Thursday are forecast between 30 and 70 mm, though certain areas could see over 100 mm. Forecasters warned that sudden, intense bursts of rain could dump over 100 mm in just a three-hour window. Downpours are expected to ease slightly by Friday across southern Vietnam. General rainfall will range from 10 to 30 mm, though localized heavy storms dumping more than 70 mm remain a threat. This extended period of severe weather coincides directly with the full-moon high tides of the eighth lunar month. At the Thu Dau Mot station near the city's eastern gateway, tidal waters are projected to breach the third warning level for four consecutive days starting Thursday. The perilous combination of torrential rain and surging tides significantly elevates the flooding risk in low-lying neighborhoods and threatens severe evening traffic gridlock. Authorities have issued widespread flood warnings for urban centers, industrial zones, and low-lying coastal areas. Officials also cautioned residents to remain alert for lightning, strong wind gusts, and potential tornadoes developing within the thunderstorm cells. Torrential rains in recent days have already submerged critical infrastructure across the city. Floodwaters inundated the area beneath the Ba Son Bridge, the Hanoi Highway, the Thu Duc Market, and major arteries like Nguyen Van Linh and Le Van Luong streets. Water levels topped half a meter in several locations, stalling hundreds of vehicles. On sloped roadways, fast-moving runoff swept motorcyclists off their bikes and severely hindered travel. Evening rush-hour storms earlier this week triggered massive gridlock, trapping commuters for up to two hours on central city streets and around the critical Hang Xanh Roundabout.

picked.t: 베트남 썬푸꾸옥항공, 첫 광동체 ‘에어버스A330’ 인도 받아…내년 60대까지 기단 확대 목표
picked.body: 푸꾸옥국제공항에 착륙 중인 썬푸꾸옥항공의 첫 번째 광동체 여객기 A330. (사진=SPA) 베트남의 신생 항공사인 썬푸꾸옥항공(Sun PhuQuoc Airways)이 설립 후 첫 번째 광동체 여객기인 A330을 인도받았다. 이번 기체는 9월부터 내년 4월까지 동사가 순차 도입할 A330 8기 중 첫 번째 기체다. 썬푸꾸옥항공은 22일 성명을 통해 푸꾸옥국제공항에서 첫 A330기를 인도받았다고 밝혔다. 동사는 이번 여객기를 통해 항공 서비스 확대 및 국제선 확충을 지속적으로 전개해 나간다는 계획이다. 에어버스의 광동체 여객기인 A330은 최대 항속거리 1만3,450km로, 썬푸꾸옥항공이 추진 중인 △러시아 △카자흐스탄 △일본 △호주 등 주요 시장은 물론 유럽 여러 도시와 국제선 연결에도 큰 도움이 될 것으로 기대를 모은다. 썬푸꾸옥항공에 따르면, 이번 기체 좌석 수는 △비즈니스 20석 △프리미엄 이코노미 21석 △이코노미 206석 등 총 247석으로 구성돼 있다. 3개 등급 좌석 모두 개인용 엔터테인먼트 스크린과 기내 와이파이가 제공된다. 동사는 이번 신규 기체 외 협동체인 A321 20대를 보유하고 있는데, 연내 보유 기체를 33대, 내년에는 60대, 나아가 2030년까지는 100대까지 늘린다는 중기 목표를 세운 상태다.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘연차 미사용수당’ 미지급 시 과태료 최대 1억 동…정부 시행령
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 근로자 퇴직 시 연차휴가 미사용수당을 지급하지 않는 기업에 과태료 최대 1억 동을 부과한다. 베트남 정부는 최근 이러한 내용을 담은 노동, 사회보험 및 해외 계약직 근로자 파견 분야의 행정 위반 제재 규정을 담은 시행령 제283/2026/ND-CP호를 공포했다. 해당 시행령은 지난 10일부터 시행되고 있다. 본 시행령은 임금 관련 위반 행위에 대한 제재 규정도 포함하고 있는데, 구체적으로 제23조 제2항에 따르면, 근로자의 퇴사 또는 실직 시 연차휴가 미사용수당을 지급하지 않거나 부족하게 지급하는 경우, 사용자에게 과태료 부과를 명시하고 있다. 위반 시 과태료는 △직원 수 1~10명인 경우, 500만~1,000만 동(192~385달러) △11~50명, 1,000만~2,000만 동(385~770달러) △51~100명, 2,000만~3,000만 동(770~1,155달러) △101~300명, 3,000만~4,000만 동(1,155~1,539달러) △301명 이상 4,000만~5,000만 동(1,539~1,924달러) 등으로 사업장 규모에 따라 차등 부과된다. 특히 해당 시행령 제7조 제2항은 해당 과태료액은 개인 기준으로, 위반 주체가 조직(단체)인 경우, 과태료가 두 배로 가중된다는 점을 명시하고 있다. 위반 시 최대 과태료가 1억 동(3,849달러)에 달할 수 있는 셈이다. 해당 과태료 수준은 △징계 대상이 아니나 일시적으로 업무에서 배제된 직원에게 임금 전액을 지급하지 않는 경우 △근로계약과 다른 직무로 임시 전보 조치시켰거나 파업 중인 근로자에게 법정 임금을 지급하지 않거나 적게 지급한 경우에도 동일하게 적용된다. 또한 △임금 지급 지연 △근로계약상 명시된 임금 미지급 또는 부족 지급 △법률로 규정된 초과근무·야간근무수당·휴업수당 △근로자의 임금 사용 결정권 방해 △사용자 지정 업체의 재화·서비스 이용 강요 △근로자 임금 부당 공제 등도 유사한 제재를 받게 된다. 사용자는 과태료 납부 외 근로자에게 미지급 또는 부족 지급된 임금 전액과 기간에 따른 이자를 지급해야 한다. 이자는 행정 처분 당시, 국영상업은행들에서 발표한 요구불예금 최고 이자율로 계산된다.
